# Skill: Multi-Type Content and Preview

## Supported types

| Type | Required editor fields | Preview |
|---|---|---|
| Subject | title, explanation, category | subject card and full detail |
| Question | question, context, desired answer | question card and answer context |
| Resource | title, description, source/link, access notes | resource card with link status |
| Offer | offer, eligibility, terms, expiry | offer card with terms and expiry |
| Request | requested item/service, context, response constraints | request card with response prompt |The selected type controls labels, required fields, correction rules, and preview. Preview must not show contributor identity, history, moderation notes, private confidence, or internal records. A preview is not publication.

Each suggestion is independently actionable. After acceptance or editing, refresh only affected preview fields and re-run validation.

## Article transformation mode

Use the canonical rules in Article Transformation Policy at ../../docs/ARTICLE_TRANSFORMATION_POLICY.md.

The original and modified articles must remain complete. Never summarize or shorten them. Preserve factual names, advertiser identity, brands, products, offers, prices, locations, and technical labels, including names that are part of historical facts or scientific terminology. For advertisements, retain the factual offer and advertiser-specific information while revising only unsupported promotional claims. Remove or revise identity only when the text makes a specific identity-centered evaluative claim, such as first, best, biggest, tallest, most, leading, famous, or genius. If no such claim exists, keep the original. Biographies, company profiles, historical reports, and sports-transfer stories are edge-case tests rather than default mission examples.


## Identity-bearing article rule

Keep factual names and identity in articles about people, films, companies, organizations, and politicians. Review adjectives, superlatives, emotional wording, marketing claims, and unsupported assertions. Reframe relevant unsupported claims as attributed claims or evidence requests; do not erase facts or shorten the article.
